correctness.rationale: For A with nonscalar residue A_0, a cyclic vector shows its residue commutant is span(I,A_0). For each residue B_0=uI+vA_0, B_i-vA_i is independently in that same span, giving q^{2d+2} choices. For scalar A_0, the radical parts of B are free and B_0 must commute with all radical coefficients of A. Over k=F_q let V=M_2(k)/kI: the bracket induces an isomorphism from the exterior square of V to the trace-zero subspace, as the brackets of representatives E_11,E_12,E_21 are E_12,-E_21,E_11-E_22. This remains valid in characteristic two. A radical tuple projecting to span of dimension 0, 1, or at least 2 in V thus leaves residue commutant of dimension 4, 2, or 1 respectively. There are P=q^2+q+1 projective lines of directions in the sense of one-dimensional vector subspaces, each admitting q^{2d}-q^d tuples of projected span exactly one after allowing scalar lifts; the scalar tuples number q^d. The remainder is nonempty: two independent directions suffice for d>=2. Multiplying by the q scalar residues yields the other three rows. Weighting by size and dividing by q^{8d+8} cancels the q^{5d+2} terms since (q-1)P=q^3-1; the exact probability is q^{-6}+(q^4+q^3-q-1)q^{-2d-6}. This confirms all sizes, multiplicities, formula and fixed-q asymptotic.
residual_risks: The frozen finite checks are only over prime fields; the independent argument uses no restriction on the finite field or its characteristic. No new numerical run needed for this proof.
